ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a uniform medium, two wave sources \( S_{1} \) and \( S_{2} \) are located on the \( x \)-axis at \( x_{1}=0 \) and \( x_{2}=14\,\mathrm{m} \), respectively. At \( t=0 \), both wave sources begin to vibrate. The vibration equation of wave source \( S_{1} \) is \( y=3\sin 5\pi\mathrm{t}\,\mathrm{cm} \), and the vibration equation of wave source \( S_{2} \) is \( y=5\sin 5\pi\mathrm{t}\,\mathrm{cm} \). A particle \( P \) is located on the \( x \)-axis at \( x_{\mathrm{P}}=4\,\mathrm{m} \). It is known that particle \( P \) begins to vibrate at \( t=0.4\,\mathrm{s} \).

1. What is the wavelength of these two waves in a uniform medium?
2. What is the distance traveled by particle $P$ from $t=0$ to $t=1.5\mathrm{s}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is x/m, and the vertical axis is y/cm. S1 is located at the origin x=0, P is located at x=4 m, and S2 is located at x=14 m. Therefore, the distance from P to S1 is 4 m, and the distance to S2 is 10 m; the nearer wave source is S1. Then reason: P only begins to vibrate at t=0.4 s, indicating that the wave emitted by S1 takes 0.4 s to propagate 4 m, so the wave speed v=4/0.4=10 m/s. The angular frequencies of the vibration equations of the two wave sources are both ω=5π rad/s, so the frequency f=ω/(2π)=2.5 Hz. The wavelength λ=v/f=10/2.5=4 m. The distance from S2 to P is 10 m, so the time when the wave from S2 reaches P is t=10/10=1.0 s. The vibration of P is divided into segments: for 0≤t<0.4 s, P is stationary, and the path length is 0; for 0.4≤t<1.0 s, only the wave from S1 arrives, y=3 sin[5π(t-0.4)] cm; for 1.0≤t≤1.5 s, the two waves superpose, y=3 sin[5π(t-0.4)]+5 sin[5π(t-1.0)] cm. Because 5π(t-1.0)=5π(t-0.4)-3π, the second term is equal to -5 sin[5π(t-0.4)], and the resultant vibration is y=-2 sin[5π(t-0.4)] cm. The period T=1/f=0.4 s. From 0.4 s to 1.0 s lasts 0.6 s, that is, 1.5 periods, with amplitude 3 cm, starting from the equilibrium position, so the path length is 1.5×4×3=18 cm. From 1.0 s to 1.5 s lasts 0.5 s, that is, 1.25 periods, with equivalent amplitude 2 cm, starting from the equilibrium position, so the path length is 1×4×2+1×2=10 cm. The total path length is 18+10=28 cm.
